items.title: 1.6.2 Operations on Complex Numbers in Polar Form (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book pp. 16-18: printed heading "1.3.3 Operations on Complex Numbers in Polar Form" (out of sequence), addition/subtraction, multiplication (Example 13), division (Example 14), then Examples 15 and 16

blocks.text: 1.3.3 Operations on Complex Numbers in Polar Form

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne is heading ka number 1.3.3 likha hai, jo sequence se bahar hai: yeh 1.4.1 ke baad aata hai aur polar form wala kaam hi aage barhata hai. Hum ne number kitab jaisa rakha hai taa ke aap kitab mein dhoond saken; ghalti sirf numbering mein hai.

Is sabaq mein hum seekhenge ke polar form mein likhe complex numbers ko jama, tafreeq, multiply aur divide kaise karte hain. Pichle topic (1.4.1) mein aap ne kisi complex number ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likhna seekha tha. Ab hum dekhenge ke yeh shakal itni mufeed kyun hai. Shuru mein hi bata doon: jama aur tafreeq ke liye polar form koi khaas madad nahi karti, lekin multiply aur divide ke liye yeh jaadu ki tarah kaam karti hai. Aakhir mein kitab ki do aur misaalein (Example 15 aur 16) hain jin mein modulus, conjugate aur argument se line aur circle ki equations banti hain.
Addition and Subtraction of Complex number in Polar form

Farz kijiye \(z_1 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\) aur \(z_2 = r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\) polar form mein do complex numbers hain. Un ka jama aur tafreeq seedha aise likha ja sakta hai:
\[z_1 + z_2 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\]
\[\qquad + r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\]
\[z_1 - z_2 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\]
\[\qquad - r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\]
Yaani kitab sirf itna kehti hai ke dono ko saath likh dijiye. Is se aage simplify karne ka koi short formula nahi hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan ek baat bohat dhyan se samjhiye: polar form mein jama ka koi shortcut nahi. Moduli ko jama aur angles ko jama mat kijiye. Agar ek akela complex number chahiye to wapas rectangular form mein jaiye aur real parts alag aur imaginary parts alag jama kijiye:
\[z_1 + z_2 = (r_1\cos\theta_1 + r_2\cos\theta_2)\]
\[\qquad + i(r_1\sin\theta_1 + r_2\sin\theta_2)\]
Phir zaroorat ho to jawab ko dobara polar form mein badal lijiye.
Shortcut kyun ghalat hai? Ek misaal dekhiye: \(1(\cos 0 + i\sin 0) = 1\) aur \(1(\cos\pi + i\sin\pi) = -1\). In ka jama \(0\) hai. Lekin agar moduli aur angles jama karein to \(2(\cos\pi + i\sin\pi) = -2\) aata hai, jo bilkul ghalat hai. Aam zindagi mein bhi aisa hi hai: ek aadmi 1 km mashriq jaye aur doosra 1 km maghrib, to un ka "jama" safar unhein wapas wahin le aata hai, 2 km door nahi.
Multiplication of Complex number in Polar form

Ab asal faida dekhte hain. Farz kijiye \(z_1 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\) aur \(z_2 = r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\) polar form mein do complex numbers hain. Product ka formula nikaalne ke liye hum inhein seedha multiply karte hain aur simplify karte hain:
\[z_1 z_2 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\]
\[\qquad \times r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\]
\(r_1\) aur \(r_2\) aam numbers hain, inhein aage le aaiye (\(r_1 r_2\)). Ab brackets kholiye; har term ko har term se multiply karna hai, is liye chaar products bante hain:
\[\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2 + i\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2\]
\[+\ i\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2 + i^2\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2\]
Ab \(i^2 = -1\) lagaiye, aur real parts ko ek jagah aur imaginary parts (jin ke saath \(i\) hai) ko doosri jagah ikattha kijiye:
\[(\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2 - \sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2)\]
\[+\ i(\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2 + \sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2)\]
Ab ghaur se dekhiye: pehla bracket bilkul \(\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2)\) ka formula hai aur doosra bilkul \(\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)\) ka (neeche "Remember" dekhiye). In trigonometric identities se:
\[z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2[\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2)\]
\[\qquad + i\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)]\]

blocks.text_alt: z one times z two equals r one r two times open bracket cos of theta one plus theta two plus i sin of theta one plus theta two close bracket

blocks.text: Matlab: polar form mein do complex numbers ko multiply karne ka matlab hai un ke moduli ko multiply karna aur arguments ko jama karna, yaani \(\arg(z_1 z_2) = \arg(z_1) + \arg(z_2)\). Sochiye kitna aasan ho gaya: chaar products aur \(i^2\) ki jagah ab sirf ek multiplication aur ek jama.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text:
Upar istemaal hone wali do identities:
\[\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B\]
\[\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B\]
Product ka real part pehli identity se mil gaya aur imaginary part doosri se. Agar yeh identities abhi yaad nahi to inhein yahin likh kar yaad kar lijiye; poori unit mein kaam aayengi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is ko tasveer mein sochiye: \(z_2\) se multiply karna \(z_1\) ko \(r_2\) guna lamba kar deta hai aur usay \(\theta_2\) angle se ghuma deta hai. Jaise ghari ki sui ko lamba bhi kar dein aur aage bhi ghuma dein.
Ek ehtiyaat: rule \(\arg(z_1 z_2) = \arg z_1 + \arg z_2\) \(2\pi\) ke multiple tak sahi hai. Agar principal argument chahiye aur jama \((-\pi, \pi]\) se bahar chala jaaye to \(2\pi\) jama ya tafreeq kar ke usay range mein le aaiye.

blocks.title: Example 13
blocks.problem: Find the product of \(5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) and \(4\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\).
steps:
Given: \(z_1 = 5\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) aur \(z_2 = 4\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2} + i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\).
Find karna hai: product \(z_1 z_2\).
Tareeqa: dekhiye, dono numbers pehle se polar form mein hain. Is liye inhein rectangular mein badal kar lamba multiplication karne ki zaroorat nahi; seedha product formula lagayenge: moduli multiply, arguments jama.

r aur θ pehchaaniye
\[r_1 = 5,\quad \theta_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\]
\[r_2 = 4,\quad \theta_2 = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: har number ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) ke saath milaiye. Bracket ke bahar wala number \(r\) hai, aur \(\cos\) aur \(\sin\) ke andar wala angle \(\theta\). Yahan dono angles mein \(\cos\) aur \(\sin\) ke andar ek hi angle hai, is liye form bilkul sahi hai.

Product formula mein rakhiye
\[z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2[\cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2)\]
\[\qquad + i\sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2)]\]
jahan
\[r_1 r_2 = 5 \times 4\]
\[\theta_1 + \theta_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: yeh wahi formula hai jo humne upar derive kiya. Formula ko pehle likh kar phir values rakhna achhi aadat hai; examiner ko bhi pata chalta hai ke aap ne kaun sa rule lagaya.

Modulus aur angle simplify kijiye
\[5 \times 4 = 20\]
\[\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{3\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{9\pi}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{10\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
Is liye
\[z_1 z_2 = 20\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)\]
Kyun: fractions jama karne ke liye common denominator 6 banaya: \(\frac{3\pi}{2} = \frac{9\pi}{6}\). Phir \(\frac{10\pi}{6}\) ko 2 se cut kar ke \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) kiya.

Tasdeeq (rectangular form mein multiply kar ke)
\[z_1 = 5\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}i\right)\]
\[z_2 = 4(0 - i) = -4i\]
\[z_1 z_2 = -4i \cdot \left(\tfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2} + \tfrac{5}{2}i\right)\]
\[= -10\sqrt{3}\,i - 10i^2\]
\[= 10 - 10\sqrt{3}\,i\]
Aur \(20\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right) = 20\left(\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right) = 10 - 10\sqrt{3}\,i\). Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab, is liye hamara jawab sahi hai. Yahan \(i^2 = -1\) ki wajah se \(-10i^2 = +10\) bana.
Dhyan dein: \(5\pi/3\) range \((-\pi, \pi]\) mein nahi hai. Agar sawal principal argument maange to \(5\pi/3 - 2\pi = -\pi/3\) lijiye; yaani yahi jawab \(20\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\) bhi likha ja sakta hai. Kitab ka jawab \(5\pi/3\) wala bhi sahi hai, kyun ke dono ek hi direction hain.

blocks.text: Division of Complex Number in Polar Form

Ab division. Farz kijiye \(z_1 = r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)\) aur \(z_2 = r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)\) polar form mein do complex numbers hain. Division ka formula denominator ko rationalize (yaani neeche se \(i\) khatam) kar ke nikaalte hain. Zaahir hai \(z_2 \ne 0\) hona chahiye, is liye \(r_2 \ne 0\):
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{r_1(\cos\theta_1 + i\sin\theta_1)}{r_2(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2)}\]
Numerator aur denominator dono ko \(\cos\theta_2 + i\sin\theta_2\) ke conjugate, yaani \(\cos\theta_2 - i\sin\theta_2\), se multiply kijiye. Yeh wahi trick hai jo aap rectangular form mein division ke liye karte aaye hain. Har hissa alag alag hal karte hain.
Denominator:
\[\cos^2\theta_2 - i^2\sin^2\theta_2\]
\[= \cos^2\theta_2 + \sin^2\theta_2 = 1\]
Dekhiye, denominator bilkul 1 ban gaya, kyun ke \(-i^2 = +1\) aur \(\cos^2 + \sin^2 = 1\). Yahi conjugate ka kamaal hai.
Numerator:
\[\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2 - i\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2\]
\[+\ i\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2 - i^2\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2\]
\[= (\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2 + \sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2)\]
\[\ + i(\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2 - \cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2)\]
Pehla bracket \(\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2)\) hai aur doosra \(\sin(\theta_1 - \theta_2)\) (neeche "Remember" dekhiye). In trigonometric identities se:
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}[\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2)\]
\[\qquad + i\sin(\theta_1 - \theta_2)]\]

blocks.text_alt: z one over z two equals r one over r two times open bracket cos of theta one minus theta two plus i sin of theta one minus theta two close bracket

blocks.text: Matlab: do complex numbers ko divide karne par jawab ka modulus un ke moduli ka quotient (taqseem) hota hai, aur jawab ka argument un ke arguments ka farq, yaani \(\arg\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right) = \arg(z_1) - \arg(z_2)\). Yaad rakhne ka aasan tareeqa: multiply ke ulat divide, aur jama ke ulat tafreeq.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text:
Division mein istemaal hone wali identities:
\[\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B\]
\[\sin(A - B) = \sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B\]
Aur denominator 1 is liye bana kyun ke \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\). Dhyan dijiye: \(A + B\) wali identities mein \(\cos\) ke saath minus tha, yahan \(A - B\) mein plus hai.

blocks.title: Example 14
steps:
Given: \(z_1 = \frac{2}{7}\left(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\), \(z_2 = \frac{3}{5}\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + i\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\).
Find karna hai: \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}\).
Tareeqa: dono polar form mein hain, is liye quotient formula lagayenge: moduli divide, arguments tafreeq (subtract). Pehle wala angle minus doosre wala angle, order ka khaas khayal.

r aur θ pehchaaniye
\[r_1 = \dfrac{2}{7},\quad \theta_1 = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\]
\[r_2 = \dfrac{3}{5},\quad \theta_2 = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: har number ko \(r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\) se milaya. \(\theta_2\) ka minus sign saath rakhiye; yahi sign aage chal kar sab se zyada ghaltiyan karwata hai.

Quotient formula mein rakhiye
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}[\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2)\]
\[\qquad + i\sin(\theta_1 - \theta_2)]\]
jahan
\[\dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{3}\]
\[\theta_1 - \theta_2 = \dfrac{7\pi}{6} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: kisi fraction se divide karna us ke ulte (reciprocal) se multiply karna hai, is liye \(\frac{3}{5}\) se divide karna \(\frac{5}{3}\) se multiply karna hai. Aur angle ke liye \(\theta_2\) ko bracket samet likha, taa ke sign na khoye.

Modulus aur angle simplify kijiye
\[\dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{10}{21}\]
\[\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6} + \dfrac{3\pi}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{10\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
Is liye
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{10}{21}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)\]
Kyun: negative angle ko tafreeq karna use jama karna hai: \(-(-\pi/2) = +\pi/2\). Phir common denominator 6 bana kar jama kiya.
Dhyan dein: bohat se students yahan \(\frac{7\pi}{6} - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) likh dete hain, yaani minus ka minus bhool jaate hain. Bracket lagane se yeh ghalti nahi hoti.

Tasdeeq (rectangular form mein divide kar ke)
\[z_1 = \tfrac{2}{7}\left(-\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}i\right) = -\tfrac{\sqrt{3} + i}{7}\]
\[z_2 = \tfrac{3}{5}(0 - i) = -\tfrac{3}{5}i\]
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{5(\sqrt{3} + i)}{21i}\]
\[= \dfrac{5(\sqrt{3} + i)(-i)}{21}\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{21} - \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{21}i\]
Aur \(\frac{10}{21}\left(\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right) = \frac{5}{21} - \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{21}i\). Dono barabar hain, is liye kitab ka jawab sahi hai. (Yahan \(\frac{1}{i} = -i\) use hua, kyun ke \(i \cdot (-i) = -i^2 = 1\).) Principal argument chahiye ho to: \(5\pi/3 - 2\pi = -\pi/3\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab yahan Examples 15 aur 16 deti hai. In mein polar formulas nahi lagte; yeh \(z = x + iy\) ke saath modulus, conjugate aur argument ki practice hain, aur in se ek line aur ek circle ki equation banti hai. In ka bunyaadi idea ek hi hai: koi bhi shart jo \(z\) par lagi ho, \(z = x + iy\) rakh kar usay \(x\) aur \(y\) ki equation bana do; phir woh equation batati hai ke aise saare points plane mein kahan hain.

blocks.title: Example 15
blocks.problem: If \(z = x + iy\), then write the equation \(|3z - i| = |3\overline{z} + 7|\) in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
steps:
Given: \(|3z - i| = |3\overline{z} + 7|\) ... (i), aur \(z = x + iy\).
Find karna hai: yahi equation sirf \(x\) aur \(y\) ki shakal mein.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhiye ke dono taraf modulus hai. Modulus nikaalne ke liye number ka \(a + ib\) form mein hona zaroori hai, kyun ke formula \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) hai. Is liye dono sides ko pehle \(a + ib\) bana kar modulus lenge, phir square kar ke simplify karenge.

Left side
\[3z - i = 3(x + iy) - i\]
\[= 3x + i(3y - 1)\]
\[|3z - i| = \sqrt{(3x)^2 + (3y - 1)^2}\]
Kyun: \(z\) ki jagah \(x + iy\) rakha, phir real part \(3x\) aur imaginary part \(3y - 1\) alag kiye. \(-i\) imaginary hissa hai, is liye woh \(3y\) ke saath jaata hai, \(3x\) ke saath nahi.

Right side
\[\overline{z} = x - iy\]
\[3\overline{z} + 7 = 3x - 3iy + 7\]
\[= (3x + 7) + i(-3y)\]
\[|3\overline{z} + 7| = \sqrt{(3x + 7)^2 + (-3y)^2}\]
Kyun: conjugate (jora, jis mein sirf imaginary part ka sign ulat jaata hai) ka matlab \(\overline{z} = x - iy\). Is ko real axis mein aaine ka aks (mirror image) samjhiye. 7 real number hai, is liye woh \(3x\) ke saath jud gaya.

(i) mein rakhiye aur dono taraf square kijiye
\[\sqrt{(3x)^2 + (3y - 1)^2} = \sqrt{(3x + 7)^2 + (-3y)^2}\]
\[(3x)^2 + (3y - 1)^2 = (3x + 7)^2 + (-3y)^2\]
Kyun: square karne se square roots khatam ho jaate hain. Dono sides non-negative hain (modulus kabhi negative nahi hota), is liye square karne se koi jawab na zyada hota hai na kam.

Khol kar simplify kijiye
\[9x^2 + 9y^2 - 6y + 1\]
\[= 9x^2 + 42x + 49 + 9y^2\]
\[-6y + 1 = 42x + 49\]
\[-6y = 42x + 48\]
\[y = -7x - 8\]
Kyun: \((3y - 1)^2 = 9y^2 - 6y + 1\) aur \((3x + 7)^2 = 9x^2 + 42x + 49\) (formula \((a \pm b)^2 = a^2 \pm 2ab + b^2\)). Ab \(9x^2\) aur \(9y^2\) dono taraf hain, is liye cancel ho gaye. Phir 1 ko right le gaye aur aakhir mein \(-6\) se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: \((-3y)^2 = 9y^2\) hai, \(-9y^2\) nahi; square hamesha positive.

Tasdeeq
Line par ek point lijiye: \(x = -1\), to \(y = -7(-1) - 8 = -1\), yaani \(z = -1 - i\).
\[3z - i = -3 - 4i,\quad |{-3} - 4i| = 5\]
\[3\overline{z} + 7 = 4 + 3i,\quad |4 + 3i| = 5\]
Dono taraf 5 aaya, bilkul jaisa hona chahiye tha. Matlab: equation \(y = -7x - 8\) complex plane mein ek seedhi line (straight line) hai; is line ka har point given shart poori karta hai.

blocks.title: Example 16
blocks.problem: Show that \((x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 8\) if \(\arg\left(\frac{z + 2i}{z - 2i}\right) = \frac{3\pi}{4}\) for \(z = x + iy\).
steps:
Given: \(z = x + iy\) aur \(\arg\left(\frac{z + 2i}{z - 2i}\right) = \frac{3\pi}{4}\).
Saabit karna hai: \((x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 8\).
Tareeqa: argument tab hi istemaal ho sakta hai jab number \(a + ib\) form mein ho, kyun ke \(\tan(\arg) = \dfrac{\text{imaginary part}}{\text{real part}}\). Hamara number ek fraction hai, is liye pehle denominator ke conjugate se multiply kar ke usay \(a + ib\) banayenge, phir \(\tan\) wala rule lagayenge.

z rakhiye
\[\dfrac{z + 2i}{z - 2i} = \dfrac{x + iy + 2i}{x + iy - 2i}\]
\[= \dfrac{x + i(y + 2)}{x + i(y - 2)}\]
Kyun: imaginary terms ko ikattha kiya: \(iy + 2i = i(y + 2)\) aur \(iy - 2i = i(y - 2)\). Ab upar neeche dono saaf \(a + ib\) shakal mein hain.

Denominator ke conjugate se multiply kijiye
\[= \dfrac{x + i(y + 2)}{x + i(y - 2)} \times \dfrac{x - i(y - 2)}{x - i(y - 2)}\]
Numerator:
\[x^2 - ix(y - 2) + ix(y + 2)\]
\[\ - i^2(y + 2)(y - 2)\]
\[= (x^2 + y^2 - 4) + 4ix\]
Denominator:
\[x^2 + (y - 2)^2\]
Kyun: \((a + ib)(a - ib) = a^2 + b^2\) hamesha real hota hai; isi liye conjugate se multiply karte hain, taa ke neeche se \(i\) khatam ho jaye. Upar \(-ix(y - 2) + ix(y + 2) = ix(4) = 4ix\), aur \(-i^2 = +1\) ki wajah se \((y + 2)(y - 2) = y^2 - 4\) plus ke saath aaya.
Dhyan dein: upar aur neeche dono ko ek hi cheez se multiply karna hai, warna fraction ki value badal jaayegi.

Parts alag kijiye
\[\dfrac{z + 2i}{z - 2i} = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2 - 4}{x^2 + (y - 2)^2} + i\,\dfrac{4x}{x^2 + (y - 2)^2}\]
Kyun: ab real part aur imaginary part bilkul saaf nazar aa rahe hain, aur argument wala rule lagaya ja sakta hai.

Argument use kijiye
\[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\text{Im}}{\text{Re}}\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\]
Common denominator \(x^2 + (y - 2)^2\) cancel ho jaata hai:
\[\dfrac{4x}{x^2 + y^2 - 4} = \tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1\]
Kyun: kisi bhi argument \(\theta\) ke liye \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{imaginary part}}{\text{real part}}\). Dono parts ka denominator ek hi hai, is liye divide karne par kat jaata hai. Aur \(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = \tan 135^{\circ} = -1\), kyun ke second quadrant mein \(\tan\) negative hota hai.

Simplify kijiye aur square complete kijiye
\[4x = -1(x^2 + y^2 - 4)\]
\[x^2 + 4x + y^2 = 4\]
Dono taraf 4 jama kijiye:
\[x^2 + 4x + 4 + y^2 = 8\]
\[(x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 8\]
Kyun: cross multiply kiya, phir sab terms left par laaye. Ab completing the square: \(x\) ke coefficient 4 ka aadha 2 hai, aur \(2^2 = 4\); yeh 4 dono taraf jama karne se \(x^2 + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)^2\) ban jaata hai. Yeh ek circle ki equation hai jis ka markaz \((-2, 0)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{8}\) hai.

Tasdeeq
Circle ka ek aisa point lijiye jis mein \(x > 0\) ho: \(x = \tfrac{1}{2}\), \(y = \tfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\) (kyun ke \((2.5)^2 + 1.75 = 8\)). Is ke liye \(x^2 + y^2 - 4 = -2 < 0\) aur \(4x = 2 > 0\). Yaani real part negative aur imaginary part positive: number second quadrant mein hai, aur \(\tan = 2/(-2) = -1\). Second quadrant mein \(\tan = -1\) wala angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) hi hai. Sahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 16 ke baare mein ek baareek nukta (yeh Principal Argument wale rule se juda hai). \(\tan\theta = -1\) sirf \(\theta = \frac{3\pi}{4}\) ke liye nahi, \(\theta = -\frac{\pi}{4}\) ke liye bhi sach hai. Argument \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) (second quadrant) sirf tab hoga jab real part negative ho aur imaginary part positive, yaani \(4x > 0\), is liye \(x > 0\).
Is liye: jis \(z\) ka bhi yeh argument ho, woh circle \((x + 2)^2 + y^2 = 8\) par zaroor hoga; example yahi saabit karne ko kehti hai, aur woh hum ne saabit kar diya. Lekin circle ka har point yeh shart poori nahi karta: \(x = -1\), \(y = \sqrt{7}\) ke liye argument \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) aata hai. Bilkul theek jawab yeh hai ke locus circle ka sirf woh hissa hai jahan \(x > 0\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
• Jama aur tafreeq: polar shortcut nahi; real parts alag aur imaginary parts alag jama kijiye.
• Multiply: moduli multiply, arguments jama: \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2\operatorname{cis}(\theta_1 + \theta_2)\).
• Divide: moduli divide, arguments tafreeq: \(\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\operatorname{cis}(\theta_1 - \theta_2)\), \(z_2 \ne 0\).
• Principal argument chahiye ho to jawab ke angle mein \(\pm 2\pi\) kar ke usay \((-\pi, \pi]\) mein laaiye.
• \(|\ldots| = |\ldots|\) wali equations: har side ko \(a + ib\) banaiye, modulus lijiye, square kijiye.
• \(\arg\) wali equations: fraction ko conjugate se \(a + ib\) banaiye, phir \(\tan\theta = \text{Im}/\text{Re}\), aur quadrant check.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
• Complex numbers jama karte waqt moduli aur angles jama kar dena. Angles jama karne wala rule sirf multiply ke liye hai (aur wahan moduli multiply hote hain, jama nahi).
• Angles ko divide ya multiply kar dena. Product mein angles jama hote hain, quotient mein tafreeq.
• Minus sign kho dena: \(\theta_2 = -\pi/2\) ho to \(\theta_1 - \theta_2 = \theta_1 + \pi/2\) banta hai.
• Division mein angles ka order ulta kar dena: hamesha \(\theta_1 - \theta_2\), yaani upar wala minus neeche wala.
• Example 15 mein bhool jaana ke \(\overline{z} = x - iy\) mein \(y\) ka sign badal jaata hai.
• Example 16 mein \(\tan\theta = -1\) likh kar quadrant check na karna.
